chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from al-Hakam ibn Aynan from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli who said:
He said: 'If you see the Master of this Command giving all that is in the treasury to one man, let nothing enter your heart [of doubt], for he is only acting by the command of Allah.'

key_terms.صَاحِبَ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: The Master of this Command (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the sign of the Imam's authority regarding the distribution of wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of prominent Kufi scholars, underscores the concept of *Ghayb al-Khass* (occultation of the specific) and the Imam's absolute discretion (*Ijtihad*) in distributing wealth, which is not bound by human notions of equity. It serves as a key proof for the divine authority (*Hujjiyyah*) of the Imam, reassuring believers that his actions, even if seemingly arbitrary to the masses, are executed strictly by God's command. This principle reinforces the Shia doctrine of obedience to the Imam regardless of external appearances.
